title: Remote Past a Memoir: 1951–1966

description.main: Kikuji Kawada's account of his first fifteen years as a photographer, 1951 to 1966, published by Case Publishing, Tokyo, in 2016 for the third Daikanyama Photo Fair. 192 black and white photographs, text by Kawada and an afterword by Rei Masuda in Japanese and English; softcover, 304 pages, edition of 1,000.
description.extended:
Kikuji Kawada's own account of his first fifteen years as a photographer, 1951 to 1966, published by Case Publishing in Tokyo in 2016 in an edition of 1,000 copies.

The Fine-Art Photography Association produced it as the third of its fapa books for the third Daikanyama Photo Fair, where Kawada's early pictures were the main visuals. Its 192 black and white photographs begin with the magazine-contest work that Ihei Kimura and Ken Domon singled out when Kawada was a student, continue through the Vivo years and Chizu (The Map, 1965), and include pictures not published before. Kawada's text and an afterword by Rei Masuda, curator at the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo, appear in Japanese and English. Yoshihisa Tanaka designed the 304-page softcover, whose cover sets the Japanese title over a torn, layered wall of the kind that fills Chizu.

Kikuji Kawada (b. 1933, Ibaraki) co-founded the Vivo collective in 1959 with Shomei Tomatsu, Eikoh Hosoe, Ikko Narahara, Akira Sato and Akira Tanno. Chizu (Bijutsu Shuppan-sha, 1965) is among the most studied Japanese photobooks; MACK republished The Last Cosmology in 2015 and Chizu as a maquette edition in 2021. He was in MoMA's New Japanese Photography in 1974. The library also holds his Nazraeli One Picture Book Mask.
description.artist_bio: Kikuji Kawada (b. 1933, Ibaraki Prefecture) studied economics at Rikkyo University (1955) and co-founded Vivo in 1959. Books: Chizu (Bijutsu Shuppan-sha, 1965; reprints Getsuyosha/Nazraeli 2005, Akio Nagasawa 2014, MACK maquette edition 2021), The Last Cosmology (1995; MACK 2015), Cosmos of the Dream King (Asahi Sonorama, 1995), Japan 1951-1960 (Nazraeli, 2014), Vortex (AKAAKA, 2022). MoMA New Japanese Photography (1974); Tate Modern Conflict, Time, Photography (2014-15). Photographic Society of Japan Lifetime Achievement Award 2011. Collections include MoMA, the Met, Pompidou, Tate, SFMOMA, MOMAT.
description.exhibition_context: Published for the third Daikanyama Photo Fair, Tokyo, 2016, for which Kawada's early work was the main visual. The 2008 exhibition Remote Past: Memoir 1951-1966 at PGI, Tokyo, showed the same body of work.

notes: Shelf: Japanese. fapa book vol. 3, produced by the Fine-Art Photography Association (FAPA) for the third Daikanyama Photo Fair, 2016. Japanese title on the cover: 遠い場所の記憶：1951－1966 川田喜久治. Case Publishing's page spells the afterword author Rei Matsuda; PGI and L. Parker Stephenson give Rei Masuda (MOMAT curator), used here.
